To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

plasma membrane enriched fraction of rat mesenteric artery was obtained by an improved method, and that this plasma membrane fraction was enriched in 5′-Nucleotidase and alkaline phosphatases, and was able to transport calcium across the plasma membrane via an ATP-dependent transport process.
the plasma membrane of rat mesenteric artery contains ATP-dependent calcium transport system and that the plasma fraction is enriched in plasma membrane marker activities.

plasma membrane isolated from rat mesenterie arteries by our improved method is free from contamination by other membrane fragments and is enriched in 5'-nucleotidases and ATP-dependent calcium extrusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation of plasma membrane from vascular smooth muscle and the characterization of the membrane in terms of morphological, enzymatic, and functional properties.
the characterization of the plasma membrane from rat mesenteries and the functional properties of plasma membranes in the regulation of intracellular calcium in the vascular smooth muscle.
a method for the isolation of a plasma membrane fraction which is highly enriched with respect to smooth muscle cell plasma membrane.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the procedure described in the present study has been successful in isolating a plasma membrane enriched fraction from rat mesenterie arteries with minimal contamination of other membrane fragments.
the plasma membrane isolated from the rat mesenteric artery contains the functional property of the calcium extrusion across cell membrane.
the plasma membrane isolated by this improved procedure is free of significant contamination by other intramembrane fragments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the plasma membrane of the smooth muscle cell is a major determinant of vascular smooth muscle tone and is a target for pharmacologic agents.
the plasma membrane of smooth muscle cells is a highly specialized membrane and that its function is to regulate the intracellular calcium.

the plasma membrane enriched fraction from rat mesenteries is suitable for the study of the calcium transport mechanism in vascular smooth muscle, and that the calcium extrusion process is an energy dependent process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to show that the plasma membrane of the vascular smooth muscle cell is capable of accumulating Ca2+ in an energy-dependent manner.
we were able to show that the plasma membrane is responsible for calcium extrusion from the cell.
the plasma membrane enriched fraction from rat mesenterie arteries can be used for the investigation of the functional properties of plasma membranes of smooth muscle cells in the vascular system.
